l: It is the policy of the Fort Worth Police Department to use Gun Shot Detection (GSD) for official law enforcement purposes that will promote the health, safety, and welfare of residents, officers, and visitors, consistent with legal and constitutional limitations, privacy concerns, and accepted ethical standards. The purpose of this order is to establish procedures for the response and investigation into violent crimes and incidents involving gunfire, while safeguarding all civil liberties.
1. Gun Shot Detection (GSD) system - Technology that detects outdoor audible gunfire within the coverage area using acoustic sensors capable of pinpointing the accurate location of a gunfire event.
2. Coverage Area - A defined perimeter where the gun shot detection system sensors can reliably triangulate incidents of gunfire.

B. The Real Time Crime Center (RTCC) will monitor all gun shot detection alerts and attempt to verify the legitimacy of each alert. RTCC will initiate a “shots fired in area” (SIG 77) for any alerts that can be verified through audio, video, or other sources.
1. If RTCC personnel feel that the call requires a more immediate response, the officer can elevate the call to priority 1 with additional information to be provided to responding officers.
C. RTCC personnel shall provide the responding officers with a location of the suspected gunfire.
D. Responding officers should take a safe and strategic approach to the incident, being aware that an offender or multiple offenders may be on scene.
E. Responding officers should consider requesting necessary resources to the scene, such as Directed Response, Air Support, and/or drone assets.
F. Responding officers shall follow any relevant procedures in the investigation to include General Order 329.00, Person with a Gun, and General Order 302.00, Active Shooter Response, as appropriate.

G. An arrest must be based on the totality of circumstances gathered from a thorough investigation and reaching the threshold of probable cause; therefore, officers shall not arrest solely on a gun shot detection alert. The gun shot detection alert is a lead only; any possible connection or involvement of any subject to the gun shot detection alert must be determined through further investigation and investigative resources.

H. Responding officers should canvas within one hundred (100) feet of the gun shot detection location for victims, witnesses, and evidence. Any casings, firearms, and magazines recovered on the scene shall be considered evidentiary.
I. Responding officers shall notify the RTCC should it become clear that the gun shot detection alert was false.
J. If an Incident Report is generated, the officer shall designate within the report narrative that the incident is Gun Shot Detection-related.
